correctness.rationale: For \(T(a,b)=(a+b,ab)\), the identity \(T^2(1,x)=(1,x+x^2)\) holds in characteristic two. For every odd \(s>1\), the trace-zero space \(W\) of \(\mathbb F_{2^s}\) has positive dimension and the linearized map \(g(x)=x+x^2\) is bijective on \(W\); each nonzero element is periodic with length greater than one. For degrees divisible by four, an explicit eight-cycle over \(\mathbb F_{16}\) embeds. These cases cover all \(m\ge3\), and \(\mathbb F_2,\mathbb F_4\) are settled by complete small-field case analysis. The standalone exact checker corroborates the finite witnesses and enumerates degrees \(1\) through \(8\); the infinite proof is not an enumeration.

Multiple actual published-finding corpus and web searches found no implying theorem; absence of search hits is not absolute priority proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete infinite-parameter solution of the characteristic-two portion of Hypothesis 6.1 from the motivating recent paper. It replaces isolated finite computations through degree \(13\) by a uniform proof, including arbitrary large prime extension degrees, and supplies a reproducible \(\mathbb F_{16}\) cycle for every degree divisible by four. This closes a natural structural gap rather than evaluating an arbitrary finite invariant.
